$comment: P0-06 — the certified main-branch protection contract for the Bizosto marketing website.
This is the website half of the certification whose ERP half lives in
lacreativodesign/nextjs-boilerplate. The two are deliberately SEPARATE files verified by
SEPARATE workflows, each running inside the repository it certifies, under that
repository's own job token.
That separation is the point. This repository is PRIVATE, and a job token issued to the
ERP repository cannot read it — GitHub answers 404. A cross-repository read that fails
must never be reported as a successful certification, so neither repository vouches for
the other.
It holds no credential.
STILL OPEN, AND STILL DELIBERATE — the ruleset existing does not close this.
The live ruleset now enforces everything else, but required_approving_review_count is
0 because this repository has exactly ONE account with any access, and that account
authors every pull request. GitHub does not let an author approve their own, so raising
the count to 1 would not add a review - it would stop anything merging.
Closing it is a two-step owner action, in this order, never the second alone:
1. grant a second human WRITE access to THIS repository (the ERP repository needs
its own separate collaborator; they do not share one);
2. set required_approving_review_count to 1 AND set certifiedFloor to 1 here.
gapOpen keeps step 2 honest: the certification suite refuses to let it go false while
certifiedFloor is still 0, so the gap cannot be closed on paper alone.
The only check REQUIRED on this repository, and deliberately so.
`Vercel` arrives as a commit STATUS rather than a check run, and it is the check this
repository actually produces for its deployments. The P0-06 certification workflow this
change adds also reports, but it is NOT required and must not become required: it reads
the live ruleset, so requiring it would let a broken ruleset block the pull request that
repairs it.
Integration id 8329 is the Vercel app. The live ruleset was read on 2026-09-17 and
carries exactly this context and id.
APPLIED AND LIVE as of 2026-09-17: ruleset 23581080, verified by direct authenticated
read of GET /repos/lacreativodesign/bizosto-website/rulesets/23581080. Every field below
was confirmed against that response, including bypass_actors being explicitly present and
empty, and current_user_can_bypass being "never". It is the only ruleset on the
repository.
THE RULESET CONTROL IS GREEN. TWO OTHER CONTROLS ARE NOT.
1. VISIBILITY — OPEN. This repository is currently PUBLIC. It was published so that the
ruleset could be created at all: GitHub Free serves rulesets on public repositories
only. That is a temporary expedient and NOT the target state. This repository holds
proprietary Bizosto marketing source and must end up PRIVATE.
expectedVisibility therefore stays "private", and the verifier reports the current
public state as repository.visibility DRIFT. That failure is correct and intended; it
must not be silenced by changing the expectation. The owner action is to upgrade the
account to GitHub Pro or higher, make the repository private, and then re-verify that
the ruleset survived the visibility change.
2. INDEPENDENT REVIEW — OPEN. See requiredApprovingReviewCount above.
Because rulesetId is now known, the verifier pins the read to that id rather than
discovering the ruleset by name. Name discovery remains only as the fallback for a
repository whose id has not been recorded yet.
